Section I
The Firm · About Effectus

A high-calibre practice for the programs that cannot afford to begin badly.

Effectus specialises in the early-stage strategy and activation of complex capital programs: the stages where ambition is still abstract, options are still open, and the cost of error is still small.

Most complex programs fail quietly, long before the first shovel breaks ground: in optimistic baselines, weak sponsorship, and control frameworks already obsolete by the time they are approved. We exist to change those odds.

We are small, senior, and independent. The advisor you meet is the advisor you keep.

Our vision

Every complex program begins with a clear purpose, an honest baseline and a team equipped to carry it, so that delivery starts flawless rather than recovering.

One spine: define, mobilise, assure

Define

We lead EF-01 and EF-02: the strategic case, the preferred option and a business case built to pass Gate 1.

Mobilise

We lead EF-05: structure, controls and people stood up before Gate 4 authorises works.

Assure

We steer and assure the gates that follow, once your team holds the program.

Section II
The Challenge

Most complex projects fail before they begin.

The first 100 days set the trajectory for everything that follows. Without senior startup capability, the damage is done before construction starts.

Failure Mode 01

Governance Gaps

Teams mobilise without the decision frameworks, reporting lines or risk tolerances needed to operate at pace. Months go on basics that should exist on Day 1.

Failure Mode 02

Schedule Erosion from the Start

Weak scope definition at the gate is a proven driver of overrun (CII PDRI research). Without structured initiation, the program is behind before a sod is turned.

Failure Mode 03

Capability Mismatch

Permanent teams are often recruited after project approval, leaving a window where critical decisions are made by people not yet fully equipped to make them.

Failure Mode 04

Cost Baseline Drift

Scope creep, undefined packages, and weak controls in early phases cascade into budget overruns that compound throughout delivery. The time to lock costs in is at the start.

Why The Odds Matter
0.5%

of large capital programs (about 16,000 studied) are delivered on schedule, on budget and with the promised benefits. Only 8.5% hit budget and schedule alone.

Flyvbjerg and Gardner, How Big Things Get Done, 2023

Section IV
The Ten Principles · Practitioner Creed

Ten principles. Not abstract. Not negotiable.

The practitioner creed behind every Effectus engagement, each principle grounded in a law of physics. They sit alongside The Effectus Way™: principles for the decisions a framework cannot make for you.

I

Start with WhyGravity

Every complex program must serve a clear and compelling purpose. If the why is weak, no how will save it.

II

Build the Right TeamResonance

No plan, tool, or process outperforms the right people in the right seats.

III

Modularise Where PossibleEnergy

Big problems are solved in manageable parts. Monoliths fail monolithically.

IV

Think Slow, Act FastInertia

Planning is sacred. We do not rush it. Execution is the cadence earned by the discipline of design.

V

Validate Internally with External DataEntropy

Internal intelligence needs external assurance. Reference-class forecasting is not optional.

VI

Remain Ruthlessly FocusedVelocity

Complex programs attract noise and scope creep. The one that survives refuses them.

VII

Manage Stakeholders ProactivelyForces

Silence is not alignment. The absence of objection is not the presence of support.

VIII

Govern with DisciplineEquilibrium

Governance is not bureaucracy. It is clarity, control, and course correction.

IX

Manage Risk RelentlesslyFriction

We do not just watch risk; we hunt it. A register is a record; a hunt is a practice.

X

Plan Backwards from the GoalTrajectory

We start at the finish line. The destination defines the method, not the other way around.

These are actionable frameworks, not abstract principles. We embed them into every engagement across Define, Mobilise and Assure.

Section IX
Why Effectus

The difference between a successful program and a failed one often comes down to one decision: who starts it.

✓

We've Sat In Your Chair

Our advisors have led or directed programs valued above A$10 billion.1 We know the politics, the pressure and the fatigue because we have lived them.

✓

We Leave, By Design

Most consultants are incentivised to stay. We are incentivised to leave. Our commercial model and reputation are built on the speed and quality of our exit, not the length of our engagement.

✓

We Build for Permanence

Every tool, every system, every process is designed from day one to be run by your team without us. No lock-in, no retainer dependency.

✓

We Start Immediately

We can mobilise a lead Project Director within days and a full startup team within two weeks. The first month is spent delivering.

✓

We Are Independent

No ownership by contractors, constructors or engineers, and no downstream design or construction fee to protect. One master: the project owner.

✓

We Scale To You

One senior practitioner or a team of twelve. Engagements are calibrated to your project's size, stage, and specific gaps. You pay for what you need, not a standard package.

1 Includes UK DfT Control Period 5 (about £11bn), where Paul Callender was Programme Integration Director with a previous employer.

Why The Start Matters
<200

In CII’s validation of the PDRI for Infrastructure, 22 completed projects representing over $6 billion of constructed cost, projects that scored below 200 of 1000 before detailed design were significantly more successful than those that scored above 200.
